_purpose: The strict envelope contract for states produced after Phase 40. RESEARCH Q6 section 3 plus D-16. Changing this file is an envelope change and needs a recorded decision. v2.10 Wave 1 (41-06) added the optional `members` finding key (D-14) — a recorded decision, see SUPERSESSIONS-v2.10.md entry 007. Rollback: a scorer without this key drops `members` at `_shape_finding` and carries the representative unchanged; absorbed-member evidence is lost on rollback (accepted downgrade, test_score.py TestRollbackStateCompat). v2.11 Phase 46 (CARRY-01/02/03, CONTEXT D-01/D-02/D-04/D-06/D-08) added finding `snapshot` and `kept_open`, pass `resolved`, root `decisions` and root `fix_verdicts`; `medium_acknowledgments` stays root_required and is legacy read-only after Phase 46.
_scope: This schema proves the ENVELOPE shape is stable. It does NOT prove orchestration or rendered reports are unchanged: those are the scorer leg (test_score.py goldens), the script leg (per-script goldens), and the trace leg (plan 40-13). One of four legs.

_rollback.procedure: To run a plugin older than Phase 46 against a Phase-46-produced state, first copy the state file to `<state>.pre-downgrade.bak`, then remove exactly the keys listed in `phase46_added`: the root keys from the root object, the pass keys from every `passes[]` entry, and the finding keys from every finding in every pass. Nothing else changes: every scored field and every pass is preserved, and the `.pre-downgrade.bak` copy keeps the Phase-46 evidence (decisions, resolutions, snapshots), so re-upgrading is a copy back. The older plugin's Finalize reads only `medium_acknowledgments`, so it will re-ask about findings whose owner decision lived in `decisions`; that is the only behavioral loss and it is non-destructive.
